title: The Eleventh
epigraph: Malachus Archive, public record. Registration Day, 09:14. Every screen in Haven City held forty seconds of white light. What was said during them is reproduced here unedited.
blurb: A god interrupts its own ceremony to put its throne on the table, and three hundred people discover they were standing in the last quiet morning Haven City would get. By the time the gate closes, six climbers are the most valuable people in the city and none of them know it yet.

image.depicts: The Tower gate seen across the empty plaza before dawn — the registration wall in profile at one end, the gate rising at the other. No figures.
image.spoilerCheck: PASS. Public architecture and empty ground. No crowd, no ceremony, no climbers, and the gate is not doing anything.
image.prompt:
{{STYLE}}
PALETTE MODE: PS-1 NIGHT NOIR, at the very end of the night.

>>> COLOUR IDENTITY: PRE-DAWN INDIGO, WITH THE CITY'S NIGHT LIGHTING STILL ON. <<<
This is the only plate in the volume set before daylight and it should be
unmistakably the odd one out. Deep indigo and blue-violet sky going pale only at
one edge. The plaza's screens are still running their overnight cycle, so
MAGENTA, CYAN AND VIOLET wash across the polished stone and are doubled in it.
One vertical GOLD SEAM of Tower light at the far end, small and steady.
NOT a grey dawn, NOT a monochrome establishing shot, NOT drab. This is a lit
city at four in the morning — the emptiness is the subject, not the darkness.

>>> NO LOCATION REFERENCE IS ATTACHED TO THIS PLATE, DELIBERATELY. <<<
The library image of this square is a symmetrical daylight view, and three
attempts at this plate copied it instead of following the text. So it has been
withheld. The description below is the ONLY authority for the square, and
nothing here should be borrowed from any other picture of it.

THE SQUARE: a large public plaza at the foot of the Tower. The floor is
MIRROR-POLISHED PALE STONE and it doubles everything above it. A ring of pale
glass towers stands around the edges, and SCREENS are mounted on their faces at
several sizes and heights. A chain-post perimeter runs along the edges, and low
planters and steps break up the boundary. It holds three hundred people; right
now it holds none.

TWO STRUCTURES, AND THEY ARE AT OPPOSITE ENDS OF THE PICTURE:
- THE REGISTRATION WALL: a broad, flat, monumental PALE SLAB standing clear of
  everything else, the surface people walk up to and set a palm against. It is
  unlit, inert and blank.
- THE TOWER: gold and faceted, rising out of the far side, with an arched GATE
  of receding arches at its base standing open, and ONE NARROW VERTICAL SEAM
  of light running up it.

>>> COMPOSE ALONG THE PLAZA, NOT ACROSS IT. THIS IS NOT A SYMMETRICAL SHOT. <<<
This plate is printed across two pages and the fold of the book runs down the
exact middle of it, so anything at the centre is cut in half and lost.
LEFT THIRD:   the REGISTRATION WALL, seen from the side, edge-on.
MIDDLE:       nothing but empty polished floor, reflections and sky. This band
              is deliberately uneventful. That is its job.
RIGHT THIRD:  the TOWER and its open gate, small with distance, pushed well
              off to the side.
IF THE FINISHED PICTURE IS LEFT-RIGHT SYMMETRICAL, OR IF THE TOWER IS IN THE
MIDDLE, THE PLATE IS WRONG however good it looks. Each half must work as a
picture on its own and the two must read as one continuous view.
ZONE: shot along the axis that takes in ZONE 1, THE WALL, in profile at one end
and ZONE 4, THE GATE APPROACH, running away to the gate at the other. The
crowd floor is empty between them.

>>> SHOT SCALE: THE ONE FULL ESTABLISHING VIEW OF THIS SQUARE. <<<
This plate is allowed to show the whole plaza because it is the only one that
will. Every later plate in this location is restricted to a zone. Use the
licence: full depth, both ends, the ring of glass towers, the screens at
several heights.

CAMERA: LOW AND GROUND-LEVEL, close to the polished floor so the reflections
run the full width of the picture and the architecture towers over the viewer.

NO FIGURES ANYWHERE. Nobody crossing, nobody in a doorway, no silhouette, no
vehicle. Three hundred people will stand here in an hour and right now there is
nobody, and that is the whole picture.

THE REGISTRATION WALL is a broad pale slab seen edge-on and unlit — inert,
waiting, with nothing written on it and nobody in front of it.
THE GATE at the far end is small at this distance, standing open, gold, the one
warm thing in a cold picture.
NO READABLE TEXT ON ANY SCREEN OR SURFACE.

title.title: The Eleventh
title.epigraph: Malachus Archive, public record. Registration Day, 09:14. Every screen in Haven City held forty seconds of white light. What was said during them is reproduced here unedited.

blocks.v: Part One: The Eleventh

Not dark. White. All of them at once, the registration feed and the commercial feeds and the transit boards and the small cracked display above the plaza's water station, every screen in Rainbow's line of sight and, he would learn later, every screen in Haven City, holding a single field of white light, and out of the wall and the stone and the air came the voice again, everywhere at once, and this time it did not stop at one sentence.

"The Tower will crown one more," Seraph said. "Hear this. I say it once, to everyone, because that is how I do things. Ten carry the Oath. There will be an Eleventh. The Eleventh will be the last. There will be no Twelfth. I have finished making lords."
A sound moved through the plaza that was not quite a gasp. Three hundred people had just heard something too large to respond to.

"To the Eleventh I will give what I have given no other." A pause. The white screens flickered, steadied. "Everything. I will give the Eleventh everything. I have been holding it for a long time, and I calculate that I am tired."

The voice stopped as if a switch had been thrown, and then, quieter, in a register that sounded almost private even though it came from every surface in the city, it added: "That was more than I intended to say."
The screens went back to the feed. The plaza stood in the morning light. The registration wall held six new questions and the crowd was no longer looking at any of them.

image.shotType: Wide, the crowd from the front, lit by screens
image.caption: Three hundred people, lit white, hearing it at the same time.
image.depicts: The plaza mid-announcement — the crowd turned up toward the white screens, faces lit from every direction, nobody moving yet.
image.spoilerCheck: PASS. Shows the moment of hearing, not the reaction to it. The six climbers are not picked out and the eleventh seat is not illustrated — only the faces of people being told.
image.hardConstraints: The screens stay WHITE and carry NO text — the words are spoken, never shown. Light comes from the screens themselves, so faces are lit from many directions with no single key light. The crowd is still ATTENTIVE, not yet stunned; that comes on the next spread and must not be spent here.
image.prompt:
{{STYLE}}
PALETTE MODE: NONE. THIS PLATE IS LIT BY WHITE SCREENS AND NOTHING ELSE.

>>> COLOUR IDENTITY: BLOWN WHITE. THE WHITEST PLATE IN THE VOLUME. <<<
Every screen in the city has gone to a single field of white light at the same
moment. That white is the entire light source, it comes from many directions at
once, and it drains the colour out of everything it lands on. Faces, clothing
and stone all go pale, cool and slightly overexposed. The previous plate is
saturated indigo and magenta; this one has almost no hue at all, and the jump
between them should be violent.
Keep small pockets of deep shadow under chins, collars and arms so the plate
still has structure — bleached, not flat.

{{LOC:TOWER_PLAZA}}
ZONE: ZONE 2, THE CROWD FLOOR. The wall and the gate are not the subject and
may be barely present or absent entirely.

>>> SHOT SCALE: WIDE, BUT FROM INSIDE THE CROWD, NOT ABOVE IT. <<<
CAMERA: EYE LEVEL, STANDING AMONG THEM, as though the viewer is one of the
three hundred. Heads and shoulders cross the foreground. We are not looking
down at a crowd; we are in one.

THE SUBJECT IS FACES HEARING SOMETHING TOO LARGE TO RESPOND TO.
Fill the frame with people — dense, ordinary, every age, Human and Valari and
Synthetic mixed, all in muted earth-toned street clothes. Their faces are TURNED
UP toward the screens and lit hard by them.

THEY ARE ATTENTIVE, NOT STUNNED. Alert, listening, held still by the act of
hearing. Not yet horrified, not weeping, not recoiling, not gasping, not turning
to each other. The reaction lands on the NEXT plate and spending it here ruins
both. If a face reads as shocked, dial it back to concentrating.

>>> THE SCREENS ARE BLANK WHITE AND CARRY NOT ONE MARK. <<<
No text, no letters, no numbers, no logo, no waveform, no interface, no icon.
Just fields of flat white light at several sizes and heights around the square.
A god is speaking and the words are heard, never seen.

DO NOT PICK ANYONE OUT. No climber is identifiable, nobody is centred, nobody is
lit differently. This is three hundred people and no protagonist.

blocks.v: Rainbow had watched this ceremony for nineteen years and he understood, standing very still in the back of a crowd that had forgotten how to move, that the ceremony no longer mattered. The questions no longer mattered, not to the city, not after this. Six people had just walked up to a wall and asked a god the truest things they carried, and forty seconds later the god had put its own throne on the table in front of the whole world, and from this morning forward nobody in Haven City would be able to look at a Climber, any Climber, these six or the twenty-seven already in the Tower or the thousands who would register in the weeks to come, without doing the same arithmetic.
One seat. Last one. Everything.

Rainbow looked at the six of them standing at the wall. They had come here for answers. Every powerful thing in this city was now going to assume they had come for the seat, and the difference between those two facts was going to follow them up all thirty levels.
Unit-9911 lowered its hands and finished the Oath, because that was its job and the job was not finished, and Rainbow respected it more in that moment than he had in nineteen years.
"The Tower is open," it said again, softly, and the words meant something different now.

image.caption: One seat. Last one. Everything.
image.depicts: The plaza after the announcement — three hundred people who have forgotten how to move, the six climbers small at the wall, nobody looking at the six new questions.
image.hardConstraints: The screens are back on the standard feed. The crowd's attention is scattered and inward, NOT on the climbers. Rainbow may be a figure at the back; he is not the subject.
image.prompt:
{{STYLE}}
PALETTE MODE: PS-4 FESTIVAL NEON, running over a crowd that is not celebrating.

>>> COLOUR IDENTITY: THE ADVERTS COME BACK ON. <<<
The plate before this one is drained white. The instant the announcement ends,
every screen returns to the ordinary commercial feed, and the square floods with
MAGENTA, CYAN, ORANGE AND HOT PINK again — garish, cheerful, moving, completely
indifferent to what has just been said. The mirror-polished floor doubles all of
it. That gap between what the light is doing and what the people are doing is
the whole point of the picture, so push the colour hard and keep the faces
still.
Warm morning daylight is in the sky above, so the plate has two light systems
at once: daylight from above, commercial neon from every side.

{{LOC:TOWER_PLAZA}}
ZONE: ZONE 2, THE CROWD FLOOR, with ZONE 1, THE WALL, visible beyond it.

>>> SHOT SCALE: WIDE AND HIGH — THE OPPOSITE OF THE PLATE BEFORE. <<<
CAMERA: ELEVATED, WELL ABOVE HEAD HEIGHT, LOOKING DOWN AND ACROSS the crowd
from behind them. The previous plate was inside the crowd at eye level; this one
is above and behind it. We see backs and tops of heads, the pattern of three
hundred people who have stopped, and the wall in front of them.

THE SUBJECT IS THREE HUNDRED PEOPLE WHO HAVE FORGOTTEN HOW TO MOVE.
Scattered, inward, each one somewhere else. No two people oriented the same way.
Nobody talking to anybody. A few have half-turned toward a neighbour and not
finished the movement.

THE REGISTRATION WALL stands in front of them with SIX SMALL FIGURES at it —
distant, unremarkable, not lit differently, not centred, not picked out. NOBODY
IN THE CROWD IS LOOKING AT THEM. That is the plate: the six most important
people in the city standing unnoticed in front of a wall nobody is reading.

The screens carry the ordinary abstract feed at every size — colour and movement
and NOT ONE READABLE CHARACTER anywhere.

blocks.v: Part Two: The Dispersal
Rainbow was watching the screens cycle back to standard feed when he saw the men who did not belong.

Four of them, moving through a crowd that was still standing stunned, with the coordinated looseness that civilians did not have. Plainclothes, professional. Their spacing kept them from reading as a group to anyone not looking for a group. They were oriented toward Signal, and they had the specific focus of people who had been waiting for a particular moment and were now in it, and the moment they had chosen was this one: three hundred people rooted to the ground by a god's announcement, cover so perfect that no planner could have arranged it.
Rainbow did not move. He never moved until the odds were clear.
Signal saw them approximately two seconds after Rainbow did. It turned toward the nearest operative and its posture changed, all at once and completely, the way a machine's posture changed.

Marcus's eye saw them before his brain finished the calculation. Rainbow could tell by the way the man's hand moved first and then stopped, caught and held back, a half-second argument between the eye and the man. The man won. Barely.
The operatives did not stop at Signal's team.

image.caption: Four of them, moving through a crowd that was still standing stunned.
image.depicts: Four plainclothes Korinth operatives crossing the frozen plaza with coordinated looseness, oriented toward Signal.
image.hardConstraints: EXACTLY four operatives. Plainclothes and NOT obviously armed — the tell is spacing and purpose, not gear. The crowd around them is static. Nothing has started yet.
image.prompt:
{{STYLE}}
PALETTE MODE: PS-3 SKYLINE DAY, deliberately UNDERSATURATED.

>>> COLOUR IDENTITY: THE COLOUR DROPS OUT. <<<
The plate before this is a neon flood. This one pulls almost all of it away.
Ordinary morning daylight, muted earth-toned crowd — ochre, sand, brick, faded
blue — pale stone, and the screens reduced to soft washes in the background
rather than the light source. A quiet, plain, almost documentary picture.
THE FOUR OPERATIVES ARE THE COLDEST AND GREYEST THINGS IN THE FRAME. Not black,
not uniformed, not sinister — simply a shade cooler and plainer than everyone
around them, so the eye finds them without being told to.
ONE SMALL ELECTRIC ACCENT holds the city in it: the cracked display above the
water station at the plaza edge, throwing a little cyan on the stone. Small, off
to one side, and the only saturated thing in the picture.

{{LOC:TOWER_PLAZA}}
ZONE: ZONE 2 running into ZONE 3, THE PERIMETER — the chain posts, the water
station and the mouths of the eastern streets behind them.

>>> SHOT SCALE: MEDIUM. THREADING THROUGH THE CROWD, NOT SURVEYING IT. <<<
CAMERA: LOW, ABOUT WAIST HEIGHT, LOOKING THROUGH GAPS BETWEEN STANDING BODIES,
with out-of-focus shoulders and arms framing the shot on both sides. The last
plate was high and wide. This one is low and obstructed, as though the viewer
is watching something they are not supposed to have noticed.

{{CHAR:KORINTH_OPERATIVE}}
>>> EXACTLY FOUR OPERATIVES. COUNT THEM. <<<
Four, no more and no fewer, spread across the width of the frame at uneven
depths — one close and partly cut by the frame edge, two mid-ground, one further
back. They are crossing a crowd that is standing still.

WHAT MAKES THEM READ IS SPACING AND PURPOSE, NOT EQUIPMENT.
No uniforms, no armour, no visible weapons, no earpieces on show, no tactical
gear, no matching clothes, no masks. Ordinary street clothes in muted colours.
They are simply the only four people in the square who are MOVING, who are
moving at the SAME PACE, who hold a wider spacing than civilians do, and who are
all oriented toward the same point off-frame. They never look at each other.

EVERYONE ELSE IS STATIC. The crowd is rooted, inward, still absorbing what they
heard. The contrast between four bodies in motion and three hundred at a
standstill is the entire composition.

NOTHING HAS HAPPENED YET. No violence, no reaction, nobody has noticed them, no
weapon is out, nobody is running. This is the ten seconds before.

blocks.v: That was what Rainbow noticed first. The second and third operatives were already peeling off toward Kimo and Spark before the first one reached Signal, fanning out across the frozen crowd with the practiced spacing of people who had been briefed on all six climbers and had decided that collateral was acceptable. Spark's mechanical arm came up. Kimo's blade lit. The Devil had already moved to cover the gap between the crowd and the exit corridor and two operatives were already moving toward him.

This was not a retrieval operation. This was a sweep. And Rainbow, watching it unfold in the plaza where a god had just named a prize, understood that Korinth had known. Not the words, maybe. But something. You did not brief a sweep team on all six climbers of two unrelated teams unless the asset you wanted had become part of something larger, and thirty seconds ago the whole city had learned what the something larger was.

The first operative reached Signal and tried to take it by the arm. Signal let him get the grip before it moved, a controlled redirect that sent the man into the second operative with considerable force. Marcus put himself between two more and the crowd, the eye tracking, and his hands found angles that civilians didn't have. Spark engaged the operative on her flank with the mechanical arm and a tool Rainbow couldn't name but didn't need to. Kimo's blade cut light across the plaza stones.
"KI series!" the fourth operative shouted, backing toward the perimeter, a comm unit already at his face. "Confirmed location, registration plaza, requesting immediate support!"
That was the whole of the explanation. Korinth didn't need more than a chassis model and a grid coordinate. The rest of the sweep was apparently just convenience.

image.caption: Spark's mechanical arm came up. Kimo's blade lit.
image.depicts: The sweep breaking out — Signal redirecting the first operative, Marcus between two more and the crowd, Spark's mechanical arm raised, Kimo's blade cutting light across the stones, The Devil covering the exit corridor.
image.hardConstraints: This is ninety seconds of professionals, not a brawl. Nobody is bleeding. The blade lights the stones. Civilians in frame are getting out of the way, not being hit.
image.prompt:
{{STYLE}}
PALETTE MODE: PS-2 SUNSET EMBER, forced by one hot light source in the frame.

>>> READ THIS FIRST. FOUR ATTEMPTS AT THIS PLATE HAVE FAILED THE SAME WAY. <<<
Every one came back as a LINEUP: five characters spread evenly across the
frame, standing upright, facing each other in a ring, weapons out, nobody
touching anybody, no crowd, and an empty plaza behind them. A promotional
group shot. That is the single thing this plate must not be.

THIS IS NOT A STANDOFF, NOT A DUEL, NOT A CIRCLE, NOT A TEAM POSE, AND NOT A
ROSTER. Nobody squares up. Nobody faces camera. Nobody stands at full height
with their weight even. Nobody is waiting for anyone else to move. If any
figure in the finished picture looks like it is posing, the plate has failed.

IT IS ONE MOMENT INSIDE A PACKED CROWD, AND THE CROWD IS MOST OF THE PICTURE.
Three hundred people are standing in this square. They fill the middle
distance and the background in every direction and they are still mostly
motionless. The fighting is happening in a small torn-open pocket among them.

{{LOC:TOWER_PLAZA}}
ZONE: ZONE 2, THE CROWD FLOOR.

>>> CAMERA: DOWN ON THE STONES, ALMOST AT FLOOR LEVEL, LOOKING ALONG THEM. <<<
The near foreground is a wide sweep of mirror-polished floor carrying
reflections, and the figures rise out of it and are cut off by the top of the
frame. Legs, boots and the underside of movement are close to camera. Nothing
in this volume is shot from here. Do not shoot it at standing eye level.

>>> THE PLAZA IS LIT BY ITS OWN SCREENS AND THIS PLATE MUST SHOW IT. <<<
A fight on pale stone in daylight will come back grey and flat unless the
city is doing something, so this is not optional decoration.
The building faces around the square carry SCREENS at several sizes and
heights, all running the ordinary commercial feed, and they throw MAGENTA,
CYAN, VIOLET AND HOT PINK down into the square from many directions at once.
The floor is MIRROR-POLISHED and doubles every bit of it, so the ground the
fight is happening on is a field of broken coloured reflection rather than
grey stone. Coloured light lands on shoulders, on the backs of heads in the
crowd, and along the wet edges of the paving.
The feed is ABSTRACT SHAPE AND COLOUR ONLY — not one readable character
anywhere on any screen.
This is the same square as the earlier plates and it is a working city in
daylight: the signs stay on.

>>> COLOUR IDENTITY: THE BLADE OWNS THE PLATE. <<<
KIMO'S BLADE IS LIT and is the hottest thing in the frame — a hard ORANGE-GOLD
line throwing real light down onto the polished stone and running along it in a
long reflected streak. SPARK'S MECHANICAL ARM is the second source and it is
COLDER: sharp BLUE-WHITE arc light at the joints. Two hot colours, one warm and
one cold, against pale stone and a muted earth-toned crowd. This is the most
saturated plate in the volume.

>>> ONLY TWO CHARACTER REFERENCES ARE ATTACHED TO THIS PLATE, DELIBERATELY. <<<
Six attempts at this picture came back as a lineup of five people standing in a
row facing camera. The cause was five attached character sheets: each one is a
studio portrait of somebody standing upright and posed, and five of those
together describe exactly the poster this plate must not be.
So three of the five are described in words instead. They are meant to be small,
half-hidden or reduced to light, and at that size a silhouette and a colour are
all the identity needed. DO NOT PROMOTE THEM TO FULL FIGURES to make up for the
missing reference.

{{CHAR:SIGNAL}}
{{CHAR:MARCUS}}
{{CHAR:KORINTH_OPERATIVE}}

THE THREE WITHOUT A REFERENCE, DESCRIBED ONLY AS MUCH AS THEIR SIZE REQUIRES:
  SPARK — a woman with an obvious heavy MECHANICAL ARM of exposed brass and
    steel plating. Only that arm and part of a shoulder need to be legible.
  KIMO — a lean figure in a PLAIN dark sealed mask with a SINGLE ORANGE-GOLD
    eye, holding a lit blade. At his distance he is a dark shape at the end of
    his own light.
  THE DEVIL — a figure in an ORNATE HORNED DEMON MASK, dark clothing, no visible
    circuitry. Almost a pure silhouette at the frame edge.

>>> NOBODY IN THIS PLATE CARRIES A FIREARM. <<< Two attempts gave Marcus a gun.
He has none and never has. This is close work: hands, holds, leverage, bodies.
The only weapon in the picture is Kimo's blade, and it is far away.

>>> THE FIVE ARE NOT EQUALS IN THIS COMPOSITION. GIVE THEM A HIERARCHY. <<<
One beat is large and sharp. Two are mid-sized and partly hidden by the crowd.
Two are small, far, and read mostly as light. If all five are the same size and
all five are fully visible, you have drawn a lineup again.

NEAREST AND LARGEST, CUT BY THE FRAME EDGE — SIGNAL, MID-THROW. It has already
taken the first operative's grip and is turning the man's own weight into the
second operative. The operative is OFF BALANCE AND COMING OFF HIS FEET, arms
wide, clearly being moved rather than falling over. Machine economy: no
wind-up, no flourish, no expression. This is the beat a viewer sees first.

MID-GROUND, PARTLY BEHIND PEOPLE — MARCUS, BACK TO THE CROWD, facing outward
with an operative closing on him. He is a WALL, not an attacker: braced low,
one arm out across the civilians behind him, holding ground. We see him past a
shoulder and an arm belonging to somebody else.

MID-GROUND OPPOSITE, HALF OCCLUDED — SPARK, the MECHANICAL ARM UP AND ARCING
blue-white, engaging the operative on her flank. Only part of her is visible;
the crowd cuts across her.

FAR AND SMALL, READ MOSTLY AS LIGHT — KIMO, the lit blade drawing its line
across the stones. He is a silhouette at the end of that light. Do not bring
him forward to show off the blade; the blade does the work from a distance.

FAR AND SMALL, AT THE EDGE — THE DEVIL, planted across the mouth of the exit
corridor with two operatives moving toward him. Almost a silhouette.

>>> FOUR OPERATIVES, PLAINCLOTHES. <<< Ordinary street clothes in muted
colours, no uniforms, no armour, no visible firearms. They are distinguishable
from civilians only because they are the ones committing to movement.

CIVILIANS ARE GETTING OUT OF THE WAY AND NONE OF THEM IS HURT. Close to camera,
people are ducking, turning away, pulling someone with them, shielding a head —
all clearly unharmed and all clearly moving AWAY from the pocket. Nobody is
struck, held, bleeding or on the ground.

NOBODY IS BLEEDING ANYWHERE IN THIS PLATE. No wounds, no blood, no gore, no
bodies. This is ninety seconds of professionals and it should look like
competence under pressure, not like a brawl.

blocks.v: Ninety seconds. Four operatives down or retreating.
But Rainbow was looking past the fight toward the streets that fed into the plaza from the east, and the second wave was already moving. More of them. Better spaced. Moving faster.

Marcus saw it at the same moment Spark did. Rainbow watched them both stop, a fraction of a second, taking in the same count of incoming bodies and the same count of available exits and arriving at the same answer. Marcus looked at the gate. Spark looked at the gate. Marcus looked at Spark. Spark looked back at Marcus. Whatever passed between them in that look had no friendship in it and no trust, just two people who had each done the math and come up with the same number.
Spark gave the smallest nod Rainbow had ever seen.
Marcus turned toward the Tower.
The Tower gate was behind them.

Rainbow had stood in front of that gate more times than he could count. The Prism sat at the end of the approach road and the gate was visible from the door on clear mornings, enormous and gold-lit, the geometric lines of it layered back in receding arches of light the way a cathedral was layered, except a cathedral invited you in and the Tower gate simply stood open and let you decide. It had always been open. It required only that you want to go through, and most people, when they stood in front of it, found out that wanting was the hardest part.

image.caption: Whatever passed between them in that look had no friendship in it and no trust.
image.depicts: Marcus and Spark looking at each other across the plaza, having each done the same arithmetic. Spark giving the smallest possible nod.
image.hardConstraints: No warmth. Two strangers arriving at the same number. The nod is nearly invisible. The second wave is visible in the background at the eastern streets.
image.prompt:
{{STYLE}}
PALETTE MODE: PS-3 SKYLINE DAY, drained almost to grey.

>>> COLOUR IDENTITY: THE QUIETEST PLATE IN THE VOLUME. <<<
The plate before this is the loudest and most saturated in the book. This one
answers it by taking everything away. Flat, cool, desaturated daylight. The
plaza behind them is reduced to unreadable soft shapes with no colour worth
naming.
ONLY TWO THINGS CARRY COLOUR: the BLUE-WHITE gleam of Marcus's cybernetic eye,
and one small COLD point of light at Spark's mechanical arm, now lowered and
quiet. Everything else is value alone.

>>> SHOT SCALE: LONG LENS, TIGHT TWO-SHOT. THE PLAZA IS GONE. <<<
CAMERA: EYE LEVEL, LONG LENS, DEPTH CRUSHED. Marcus and Spark are on opposite
sides of a wide square and this shot compresses that distance until they read as
close together — two heads and shoulders, large in frame, one at each side.
NO ARCHITECTURE. No wall, no gate, no Tower, no screens, no stone floor
receding. The background is soft unreadable movement and nothing a viewer could
use to work out where they are. Every other plate in this square has shown the
square. This one refuses.

{{CHAR:MARCUS}}
{{CHAR:SPARK}}
EXACTLY TWO FIGURES IN FOCUS, AND THEY ARE LOOKING DIRECTLY AT EACH OTHER
ACROSS THE FRAME. Nobody else is sharp.

>>> THERE IS NO WARMTH IN THIS. <<<
Not a moment of connection, not relief, not respect, not the beginning of a
friendship. Two strangers have separately counted the same incoming bodies and
the same available exits and arrived at the same number, and each has noticed
that the other got there too. Read it as ARITHMETIC, not feeling. Both faces are
flat, hard and businesslike.

SPARK'S NOD IS ALMOST INVISIBLE. A fraction of an inch, chin barely dropped,
already finishing as we see it. Do not draw a nod that a viewer could describe.
If it reads as a greeting, it is far too big.

IN THE FAR BACKGROUND, SOFT AND UNTHREATENING IN SCALE: the SECOND WAVE entering
from the eastern streets — more figures than before, better spaced, moving
faster. Small, blurred, and unmistakably additional. They are the reason for
the look, not the subject of the plate.

blocks.v: The six of them crossed the plaza toward it at a run, the second wave closing behind them. The civilian operatives slowed at the approach to the gate perimeter. They didn't stop. They were professionals. But they slowed, and the slowing was not a tactical decision. It was the deep, involuntary response of people who had grown up in Haven City and absorbed what the Tower meant through years of watching people walk through that gate and not come back. The gate was open and the gate had always been open and walking through it was a choice and the choice was permanent.
The six climbers did not slow.

The gate took them and they were gone, the gold light closing behind the last of them like a curtain, and then there was only the gate standing open in the morning air, burning, as it always burned, as if waiting for the next person to decide.

The second wave stopped at the perimeter. Stood there for a moment. Then the senior operative said something into his comm and they began to reorganize, because you could not follow registered climbers into the Tower and Korinth, whatever else it was, understood the rules of Haven City.
Rainbow turned and walked back toward The Prism by the long route.

image.caption: The gate took them and they were gone.
image.depicts: The Tower gate — enormous, gold-lit, geometric lines layered back in receding arches — with the last of the six passing through and the gold light closing behind them like a curtain.
image.hardConstraints: The gate is OPEN and has always been open; it does not have doors that shut. The operatives have stopped at the perimeter and are not following. Figures read as silhouettes against the gold.
image.prompt:
{{STYLE}}
PALETTE MODE: PS-2 SUNSET EMBER, pushed to pure gold.

>>> COLOUR IDENTITY: GOLD. THE BRIGHTEST PLATE IN THE VOLUME. <<<
The plate before this is drained to grey. This one is molten. GOLD fills the
opening, floods down the mirror-polished approach and comes back up off it, and
every figure in the picture is a black silhouette cut out of that light. Deep
navy only in the faceted mass around the arch, to give the gold something to
burn against. Nothing muted, nothing grey, nothing cool anywhere in the frame.
After eleven plates this is the payoff of the volume's whole light system.

{{LOC:TOWER_GATE}}
ZONE: ZONE 4, THE GATE APPROACH, seen from the plaza side.

>>> SHOT SCALE: VERY WIDE. CAMERA ON THE GROUND, LOOKING UP INTO THE ARCH. <<<
The gate is ENORMOUS and the camera is low enough that it fills most of the
frame and the top of it leaves the picture. Receding arches layered back like a
cathedral, a vertical seam of white light rising out of the arch. The viewer
should feel small.

>>> THE GATE HAS NO DOORS AND CANNOT BE SHUT. <<<
No leaves, no hinges, no panels, no mechanism, no portcullis, no barrier of any
kind, nothing that could ever close. It simply stands open and it always has.
When the text says the light closed behind them, that is glare and depth — an
optical effect of looking into brightness — NEVER a door.

FIGURES, ALL AS SILHOUETTES AGAINST THE GOLD, NONE IDENTIFIABLE:
  - THE LAST OF THE SIX passing through the opening, small, already deep in the
    light, mid-stride and not looking back.
  - Behind them, at a distance, the OPERATIVES STOPPED AT THE PERIMETER. Standing
    still. Not following, not reaching, not raising anything. They have stopped
    because of what the gate is, and their stillness must read as a decision
    rather than as an obstacle stopping them.
Nobody's face is visible. Nobody is lit from the front.

NO TEXT, NO SIGNAGE, NO MARKINGS anywhere on or around the gate.

blocks.v: Part Three: The Screens Go Dark
He was halfway down the approach road when the surveillance node above the transit hub across the street went dark.

Not a power failure. The node had been running cleanly when he passed it on the way to the plaza. Now it was dark, and a thin thread of smoke rose from its housing, and as Rainbow watched, a hairline fracture appeared in the mounting bracket above it and began working its way through what should have been solid-bonded steel.

A section of paving fifteen feet ahead of him shifted, a barely perceptible subsidence, the kind of thing that happened when something underground settled. Except nothing underground should be settling here. This block had been resurfaced two years ago, per Seraph's infrastructure schedule, and Seraph's infrastructure schedules did not produce settling pavement two years later.
Rainbow stopped walking and looked at the paving and then at the node and then at the crack that was still working its way through the mounting bracket.

image.caption: A hairline fracture, working its way through what should have been solid-bonded steel.
image.depicts: The surveillance node above the transit hub gone dark, a thin thread of smoke from its housing, and a crack opening through the mounting bracket above it.
image.spoilerCheck: PASS. Grey is not depicted and must not appear anywhere in this plate. The damage is the only evidence of him.
image.hardConstraints: No figures. The crack is fine and precise, not an explosion. Smoke is a thread, not a plume. This is sabotage that looks like decay.
image.prompt:
{{STYLE}}
PALETTE MODE: PS-3 SKYLINE DAY, cool and clean.

>>> COLOUR IDENTITY: COOL GREY MORNING, ONE RED FAULT LIGHT, ONE THREAD OF SMOKE. <<<
The plate before this is molten gold filling the frame. This one is small, cold
and quiet — pale grey-blue morning light on grey armoured housing and grey
steel. The ONLY saturated thing in the picture is a single small RED FAULT LED
on the node's housing, still lit while everything else in it has died. That one
red point against all that grey is the entire colour story.

{{LOC:APPROACH_ROAD}}

>>> SHOT SCALE: CLOSE OBJECT STUDY. ONE FIXTURE, NOTHING ELSE. <<<
CAMERA: LOOKING UP AT THE NODE FROM THE STREET DIRECTLY BELOW IT, tight enough
that the housing, its curved bracket and the wall it is bolted to fill the
frame. Pale sky behind. The road, the Tower and the buildings are out of shot
almost entirely. Nothing else in this volume is framed this tightly.

>>> THE SUBJECT IS A CRACK IN A PIECE OF STEEL. <<<
Everything else supports it.
  - THE SURVEILLANCE NODE is DARK. Its lenses are dead and flat. No glow, no
    scan light, nothing running.
  - A THREAD OF SMOKE rises from a seam in the housing. A THREAD — fine, single,
    barely there, drifting straight up in still morning air. NOT a plume, NOT
    billowing, NOT a fire, no flame anywhere, no sparks, no scorching.
  - A HAIRLINE FRACTURE runs through the MOUNTING BRACKET above it, and it is
    the sharpest thing in the picture. Fine, clean, precise, travelling — a
    single line working its way across solid-bonded steel, with the metal on
    either side of it undeformed. It looks GROWN, not struck.

NO EXPLOSION. No blast, no debris, no impact mark, no burn, no bent metal, no
shattering, no shrapnel. Nothing has hit this. Something has UNMADE it from the
inside, and it must look like ordinary decay to anyone who has not been told
otherwise.

NO FIGURES AT ALL. Nobody in the street, nobody at the edge of frame, no
silhouette, no reflection of a person in the housing.

blocks.v: He had heard about the new Oath Lord. Grey, they called him. The Architect. The fastest climber in the Tower's history, forty-seven days start to finish, a number that had made every faction in Haven City sit up and recalculate, because forty-seven days suggested either extraordinary capability or extraordinary assistance and nobody could agree on which. Rainbow had his own opinion. You didn't write the code that built a god and then have that god make your climb harder than it needed to be. Seraph had reasons for what Seraph did, and Grey's reasons and Seraph's reasons had apparently pointed in the same direction. And now, fifteen months after the city gained its tenth lord, the god was announcing its eleventh and calling it the last. Rainbow did not believe in coincidences that large. He didn't know what the connection was. He knew there was one.
The mounting bracket gave way. The surveillance node dropped eight feet and caught on its cable housing and hung there, swinging slightly, dead.
Rainbow looked at it for a moment and then walked back into The Prism and locked the door behind him.

He stood behind the bar in the quiet of the morning and thought about the six people he had just watched walk into the Tower, into a climb that had meant one thing when they planned it and meant something else entirely by the time the gate closed behind them.

image.caption: It dropped eight feet and caught on its cable housing and hung there, swinging slightly, dead.
image.depicts: The surveillance node hanging dead from its cable over the approach road, Rainbow standing in the street looking up at it, the Tower behind him.
image.hardConstraints: Rainbow is small in frame and stopped mid-walk. The node hangs at an angle. Morning light. Grey is not present.
image.prompt:
{{STYLE}}
PALETTE MODE: PS-2 SUNSET EMBER, read as LOW MORNING SUN down a street.

>>> COLOUR IDENTITY: WARM OCHRE MORNING, RAKING ALONG THE STREET. <<<
The plate before this is close, cold and grey. This one opens out and warms up.
Low morning sun comes down the length of the street from the Tower end, so the
whole road is lit warm ochre and long shadows run toward the camera. The Tower
gate sits small and GOLD at the far end. Cool blue-grey shadow on the shaded
side of the street gives the warmth something to sit against.
CITY LIGHT IS STILL ON in daylight, because this is a working street: small
CYAN and MAGENTA shopfront signage along the frontages, a lit transit board at
the hub, warm interior glow behind windows. Small, but present at intervals down
both sides.

{{LOC:APPROACH_ROAD}}

>>> SHOT SCALE: WIDE. THE FULL LENGTH OF THE STREET. <<<
CAMERA: STREET LEVEL, STANDING HEIGHT, looking down the road toward the Tower.
The previous plate was a tight upward study of one fixture; this one pulls all
the way back and puts that fixture in its street.

{{CHAR:RAINBOW}}
ONE FIGURE ONLY, AND HE IS SMALL. Rainbow stands in the middle of the road at
mid-distance, perhaps a sixth of the frame height, STOPPED MID-WALK with his
weight still on one foot — a man who was walking somewhere and has stopped
because he has looked up. His head is tilted back. He is a small figure in a big
street and the street is the picture.
NOBODY ELSE IN FRAME. No pedestrians, no traffic, no Bone Patrol, no Grey.

THE SURVEILLANCE NODE now HANGS DEAD FROM ITS CABLE above the road, dropped
about eight feet from its bracket, HANGING AT AN ANGLE and slightly swinging.
The broken bracket is still visible above it. It is dark and it is clearly a
thing that has fallen and been caught.

>>> GREY IS NOT IN THIS PLATE. <<< No figure on a roof, no silhouette in a
doorway, no shape at the end of the street, nobody watching. The damage is the
only evidence of him and it must stay that way.

blocks.v: He thought about Nyx'ara first, because she had left the full glass on the table and that was the thing that stayed with him, the glass that nobody had touched. The Valari woman with her circuits suppressed low and her hands flat on the table and the grief that had come from a generation before her and lived in her body anyway. She was climbing to restore the Hive Mind. Rainbow had lived beside the Valari Quarter for nineteen years. He didn't fully understand what the Hive Mind meant to them, but he understood enough. Her question was large. The questions that came from that kind of grief were always large, and they were also almost never the real question, which was something the Tower had a way of making clear.

He thought about Signal, the Korinth chassis with Nathan Zhao inside it, and the bulletin he had been watching for three months on the commercial feed. Korinth wanted the chassis back badly enough to run a sweep at a public ceremony. That was before a god put a throne on the table. Rainbow thought about what a company like Korinth did with the knowledge that the last seat in existence had just been opened, and that their runaway asset was inside the Tower climbing toward it, and he decided the bounty number he'd memorized was about to become a historical footnote.

image.caption: The glass that nobody had touched.
image.depicts: Rainbow alone behind the bar of a locked, empty Prism in the morning light, the one full glass still on the corner table.
image.hardConstraints: The full glass is visible and is the emotional subject even though Rainbow is the figure. Door locked. Daylight in a room built for night — that wrongness is the point.
image.prompt:
{{STYLE}}
PALETTE MODE: PS-3 SKYLINE DAY indoors, which this room was never built for.

>>> COLOUR IDENTITY: DAYLIGHT IN A NIGHT ROOM, AND THE NEON IS OFF. <<<
Every other plate ever set in this bar is lit magenta and violet and amber, at
night, full of people. This one is the opposite and the wrongness is the point.
HARD COLD WHITE-BLUE DAYLIGHT comes through the front glass in defined shafts,
raking across the floor and the bar top and lighting up the dust. The room's
neon tubes and signage are DEAD AND UNLIT — still there, still coloured objects
in magenta and violet glass, but switched off and grey inside. A viewer should
be able to see exactly how much colour is missing.
The ONE surviving warm thing is the low amber standby glow of the back bar,
small and outmatched by the daylight.

>>> NO LOCATION REFERENCE IS ATTACHED TO THIS PLATE, DELIBERATELY. <<<
The library image of this bar is a NIGHT photograph with every neon tube lit,
and seven attempts at these interiors copied its light instead of following the
text. So it has been withheld. The description below is the only authority.

THE ROOM: a big, deep bar — not a small one. A long BAR runs down one side with
a row of stools, and behind it a back bar of bottles with a small SCREEN mounted
above. Opposite the bar are CORNER BOOTHS with red banquettes and one CORNER
TABLE set apart from the others. Between them is an open FLOOR, with the FRONT
DOOR at one end behind a large pane of glass. At the far end, up ONE STEP
through a wide opening, is a deeper BACK ROOM of loose tables with heavy columns
and a low ceiling. Deep navy structure throughout, warm wood and brass, red
seating.

>>> EVERY LIGHT IN THIS ROOM IS SWITCHED OFF. IT IS SHUT, IT IS EMPTY, AND IT
>>> IS THE MORNING AFTER. <<<
The neon tubes and signs are still mounted where they always are, and they are
DEAD: magenta and violet glass hanging grey and unlit, the coloured overheads
off, the back room dark. They are objects, not light sources.
The ONLY exception is one small warm AMBER STANDBY GLOW at the back bar.
COLD DAYLIGHT THROUGH THE FRONT GLASS IS THE ONLY REAL LIGHT IN THE PICTURE,
and it comes in as defined shafts that rake across the floor and catch dust.
HOW MUCH COLOUR IS MISSING IS THE POINT. If this plate looks like a nightclub,
it has failed.
>>> SHOT SCALE: MEDIUM, ACROSS THE ROOM. NOT AN ESTABLISHING WIDE. <<<
CAMERA: EYE LEVEL, FROM THE FLOOR SIDE, looking toward the bar and past it to
the corner. The next plate is the wide view of this room, so this one must not
be. Show a section of the bar, one man, and one table — not the whole room.

{{CHAR:RAINBOW}}
ONE FIGURE. Rainbow on the SERVICE SIDE of the bar, bottle shelves at his back,
counter in front of him, stools empty on the far side. He is not working. He is
standing still, looking across the room at the corner table, with the flat
attention of a man thinking about something a long way off.
His face stays IN SHADOW under the brim, as it always does, with the red right
eye burning low and steady in that shadow — even here, in daylight, the shadow
holds. Nobody else is in the room.

>>> THE EMOTIONAL SUBJECT IS A GLASS, NOT THE MAN. <<<
On the CORNER TABLE, set apart from the other tables, stands ONE FULL GLASS.
Untouched, filled to the shoulder exactly as it was poured. A shaft of daylight
falls across it and it is the brightest, cleanest object in the picture.
Compose so the eye lands on the glass. Everything else in the room is used —
stools pushed out, cloths, empties waiting — and that one glass is not.

THE FRONT DOOR IS SHUT AND LOCKED, and the street beyond the glass is bright and
empty.

blocks.v: He thought about the second team more briefly. Kimo Tomiko, whose three words at the wall had not really been a question. He had already decided the answer. He was climbing to hear a god agree with him. Spark and the mechanical arm she had chosen when she didn't have to, and a question about outliving herself that meant she had already done the math on her own absence and accepted the result. And Tal'Voss, who was now The Devil, who had discarded a lineage in front of every screen in the city. He had not been angry at the wall. He had been finished, and in Rainbow's experience finished lasted longer than angry.
Then he thought about Marcus.

He came back to Marcus the way he had kept coming back to him all night. The eye that wouldn't stop. The five words at the wall. The way Marcus had stood there, like a man reporting for duty. Asking a god for help was easier for a man like that if he treated it as a mission.
How do I make it stop.

image.caption: Finished lasts longer than angry.
image.depicts: The empty Prism with the six vacated places along the bar and at the tables, morning light across them.
image.spoilerCheck: PASS. No climbers depicted — they are in the Tower. This is their absence.
image.hardConstraints: No figures at all, or Rainbow only as a reflection. The six places should be readable as six. Quiet.
image.prompt:
{{STYLE}}
PALETTE MODE: PS-3 SKYLINE DAY, and this plate is where the bar earns its name.

>>> COLOUR IDENTITY: THE SPECTRUM. THE ONLY PLATE OF ITS KIND. <<<
Above the entrance of this building is a TRIANGULAR FACETED WINDOW. With the sun
low and the room empty, that window does what a prism does: it throws a clean
BAND OF SPECTRUM — red, orange, gold, green, cyan, violet — in a long diagonal
across the floor, up over the bar top and along the empty stools. Sharp-edged
and deliberate, not a haze and not a lens flare. Draw it as a solid ribbon of
separated colour lying on real surfaces.
Everything the band does not touch is quiet: pale grey-blue morning, dead unlit
neon, warm wood and brass. So the room is mostly cool and still, with one stripe
of full colour running through it.
The plate before this one is cold and nearly colourless. This is the answer.

>>> NO LOCATION REFERENCE IS ATTACHED TO THIS PLATE, DELIBERATELY. <<<
The library image of this bar is a NIGHT photograph with every neon tube lit,
and seven attempts at these interiors copied its light instead of following the
text. So it has been withheld. The description below is the only authority.

>>> IS THE MORNING AFTER. <<<

The ONLY exception is one small warm AMBER STANDBY GLOW at the back bar.
COLD DAYLIGHT THROUGH THE FRONT GLASS IS THE ONLY REAL LIGHT IN THE PICTURE,
and it comes in as defined shafts that rake across the floor and catch dust.
HOW MUCH COLOUR IS MISSING IS THE POINT. If this plate looks like a nightclub,
it has failed.
>>> SHOT SCALE: WIDE, THE LENGTH OF THE ROOM. THE ONE FULL VIEW. <<<
CAMERA: HIGH — well above head height, looking DOWN the length of the room. The
previous plate is at eye level across the room; this one is above it and along
it. From up here the floor, the bar top and the seats all read at once.

>>> NO PEOPLE. NONE. <<<
Not a figure, not a silhouette, not a shadow of one, not someone through the
window. Rainbow may appear ONLY as a small reflection in the back-bar mirror or
in the glass, and it is better if he does not appear at all. The room is empty
and its emptiness is the entire subject.

>>> SIX PLACES, AND A VIEWER MUST BE ABLE TO COUNT THEM. <<<
Six spots in this room have just been vacated, and each one is marked by what
was left behind: a stool pushed back at an angle, a chair turned out from a
table, a used glass, a cloth, a coaster, a coat hook empty. SPREAD THEM OUT —
some along the bar, some at the tables — with clear space between so that a
reader counts SIX without effort. Not five, not seven.
The rest of the room is squared away, clean and ready, which makes the six read
as deliberate rather than as mess.

QUIET. No movement, no dust storm, no drama. A room the morning after, holding
still.

blocks.v: Five words. Rainbow had heard a hundred questions at a hundred registration ceremonies. He had never heard one that sounded so much like a man asking for a way out. And now the whole city had heard it too, and the whole city was going to forget it by nightfall, because the whole city was busy asking a different question, the one Seraph had planted in three hundred thousand heads at once: who gets everything?
Six people had gone up the Tower carrying honest questions, and the world below them had already decided they were carrying a crown.
Rainbow raised his glass toward the empty street outside.

Behind him, the small screen above the back bar, which had been cycling the standard feed, stuttered. One frame of white. One word, in the voice that was not loud so much as everywhere, quiet now, almost to itself:
"Everything."
Then the feed came back, a vendor advertising boots, and the morning went on.
Rainbow drank, and went back to work.

image.caption: One frame of white. One word.
image.depicts: The small screen above the back bar caught in its single white frame, Rainbow's raised glass in the foreground.
image.hardConstraints: ONE screen, white, mid-stutter. NO text or lettering on it — the word is spoken, not shown. The glass is raised toward the empty street. Rainbow's face may be out of frame.
image.prompt:
{{STYLE}}
PALETTE MODE: PS-1 NIGHT NOIR at the back of the room, interrupted by one white frame.

>>> COLOUR IDENTITY: ONE WHITE FLASH, AND IT IS THE FIRST SINCE THE OPENING. <<<
The plate that started this volume was drowned in white screen light. This is
the last plate and it closes the loop with a single small one. The back bar is
the deepest, warmest, darkest corner of the room — amber standby glow, brass,
dark bottle glass, deep navy shadow, well away from the daylight at the front.
Into that warm dark, ONE SMALL SCREEN has gone HARD FLAT WHITE for a single
frame. It is the brightest thing in the picture by a wide margin, it throws
cold white across the bottles and the raised glass, and it does not belong in
this warm little corner at all.

>>> NO LOCATION REFERENCE IS ATTACHED TO THIS PLATE, DELIBERATELY. <<<

and seven attempts at these interiors copied its light instead of following the
text. So it has been withheld. The description below is the only authority.

THIS PLATE IS THE EXCEPTION TO THE DAYLIGHT ABOVE ONLY IN WHERE IT LOOKS: it
is jammed into the back-bar corner, the deepest and warmest part of the room,
far from the front glass. Amber standby glow, brass and dark bottle glass. The
daylight is somewhere behind camera and does not reach here. The neon is still
off.
>>> SHOT SCALE: CLOSE. THE TIGHTEST PLATE IN THE VOLUME. <<<
CAMERA: LOW AND NEAR, just above the bar top, so the raised glass is large in
the foreground and the small screen sits behind and above it. NO ROOM. No floor,
no stools, no booths, no far wall, no daylight shafts. The previous plate is the
wide high view of this room; this one shows a few feet of back bar and nothing
else.

>>> TWO OBJECTS. THAT IS THE WHOLE PICTURE. <<<
  1. A RAISED GLASS in the near foreground, held up and slightly forward, angled
     toward the bright empty street somewhere off-frame. It catches the white
     from the screen along one edge and the amber from the back bar along the
     other. It is not a full glass and it is not empty.
  2. THE SMALL SCREEN above the back bar, mid-stutter, HELD ON ONE FRAME OF FLAT
     WHITE LIGHT.

>>> THE SCREEN IS BLANK WHITE AND CARRIES NOT ONE MARK. <<<
No word, no letter, no character, no caption, no logo, no waveform, no interface
element. A god says one word and the word is heard, never seen. If anything
readable appears on that screen the plate has failed.

{{CHAR:RAINBOW}}
RAINBOW IS PRESENT ONLY AS A HAND AND A FOREARM holding the glass, and at most
the edge of a shoulder. HIS FACE IS OUT OF FRAME ENTIRELY. Do not show his head,
his hat or his eye. The plate is the glass and the screen.
